items.excerpt: Argues that collapsing every AI agent into a chat box is a design failure: over-simplified conversational interfaces hide state, options and control that designers should be surfacing. A craft-level critique of the default AX pattern and what should replace it.

Proposes Design.md as a single machine- and human-readable source of truth for a brand's visual identity, so AI agents build from real tokens and conventions instead of falling back to generic components. A concrete design-system-for-agents pattern.

As AI agents increasingly 'read' interfaces before humans do, the piece rethinks who a designer's real audience is and how frameworks built for human eyes must adapt when a machine proxy sees the design first.

A widely-shared walkthrough (875+ likes) of packaging design principles into a reusable 'skill' file that measurably improves an AI coding assistant's visual output — turning vague vibe-coded UIs into brand-consistent design. Practical AX craft for designers steering agents.

A Belfast gallery's decision to exhibit AI-generated art has split the creative community; the essay weighs both sides of how generative AI is reshaping what counts as art and authorship for working creatives. Marginal (opinion) — included for outlet diversity.
